newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen capped near 127.10 yen in Asia trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen capped near 127.10 yen in Asia trade.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be range-bound and top-heavy during Asian trading time on Tuesday, with the topside capped near 127.10 yen on expectations of exporter sales and continuing concern about possible Bank of Japan (BOJ) intervention.

Monday's surge in U.S. stocks, which sent the Dow Industrials to an all-time closing high, and greater expectations of a U.S. interest rate rise later this month are expected to keep the downside solid. Importer bids are also likely to provide some additional support, keeping the dollar tightly cemented within its range, dealers said.

The Dow surged 143 points, or two percent, to 7214, the fourth-biggest rally in point terms in the blue chip average's history. Signs that U.S. inflation remains in check, along with increased expectations that a capital gains tax cut will be enacted in the near future, supported the rally.

The stock gains suggested that an additional rate rise by the Federal Reserve may be in the offing when its policy arm meets later this month. The Fed last raised the Federal Funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent on March 25.
Tokyo dealers said trade was likely to be quiet and directionless after Monday holidays in Tokyo and London.

They added that dollar/yen was surprisingly unresponsive to a number of positive factors in recent days and that activity on Tuesday was likely to be driven more by moves in the yen crosses, particularly mark/yen.

Exporters, many of whom will be returning to the market today after extended holidays, are likely to be interested in selling, but not until the dollar is over 127 yen and the mark over 73.50 yen, a trust bank dealer said.
"Exporters won't sell until around 127 yen because it doesn't seem now as if the dollar will go below 126 yen," he added.
Some sales are also likely just below 127 yen, a city bank dealer said.

The market is expected to watch for active importer buying, which could set the stage for an attack on the 127-yen level. But dealers said rises are still difficult to predict until the market sees how London markets respond to recent moves.
